title: The Lighthouse at Kettleness Bay

source.description: Fictional test fixture; no such song exists

artist_note_verbatim: A fictional song written to exercise the storyboard tooling.

lines.text: The bay is wide and the water is grey,
and the boats are small and far away.
I climb the cliff with the wind in my coat,
counting the steps I have walked by the note.
The harbour hums with an iron chain,
and the gulls cry out the weather's refrain.
The storm comes up like a wall of glass,
and every lamp in the town goes dark as it passes.
And I light the lantern, I light it again,
I light it for the boats and for the rain.
Turn my face to the weather, turn my face to the sea,
keep a light on the headland and a light on me.

structure_as_sung_source: Fictional: the chorus is sung twice in the recording.
